task: Horizon 16 of agent-agnostic-browser-bridge: generalize captureTab's non-throwing too-large result pattern to executeScript and evaluatePage, fix findElement's duplicated size-limit constants, and add an explicit action to close the sandbox tab on request.

analysis.objective: Generalize captureTab's non-throwing, structured too-large result pattern (CaptureTabFailureResult) to executeScript and its CDP twin evaluatePage (both currently throw on oversize despite sharing one constant), fix findElement's duplicated MAX_MATCHES/MAX_TEXT_CHARS constants (a real platform constraint: the chrome.scripting-injected function cannot close over module scope, so the limits must be threaded through as call arguments), and add a new explicit closeSandboxTab page action so the extension's single dedicated tab no longer stays open indefinitely.
analysis.successDefinition: executeScript and evaluatePage both return a defined non-throwing too-large result instead of throwing, surfaced as isError:true at the MCP layer; findElement's match/text-length limits are defined exactly once (module-level) and threaded into the isolated-world function as arguments; a new closeSandboxTab action closes the sandbox tab and clears its persisted id (no-op-safe, scoped only to the sandbox tab, reusing existing capture-buffer eviction); tools/chrome-bridge's own npm run verify (tsc/eslint/vitest) is green; README and the MCP tool catalog are updated; a live-Chrome head-to-head via the chrome-bridge MCP demonstrates both the oversize isError path and the close/recreate tab lifecycle against a real running extension.
assumptions: Horizon 15 completed successfully (render-the-tab primitive shipped, full-page capture live-verified) so this horizon does not need to revisit that primitive

evaluatePage moves in lockstep with executeScript in this horizon because they currently share the exact same MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS constant and near-identical throw/error-sentinel mechanism (page-actions.ts:648-673, debugger-ports.ts:588-595); leaving only one non-throwing would be a foreseeable, avoidable inconsistency

findElement's injected function genuinely cannot close over module scope (chrome.scripting structured-clones the function reference into an isolated world) — the only mechanical fix is threading the limits through as call arguments, confirmed by a pre-implementation grep that findElement's call site is the sole invocation of that injected function

The user explicitly chose an EXPLICIT, MCP-caller-invoked closeSandboxTab action over any automatic close-on-disconnect/suspend behavior, because relay disconnects are routine/transient (bridge-client.ts auto-reconnects) and SW suspension is undetectable/already-lossy by design, and because this project has repeated precedent (horizon 2 pull-only, horizon 6 'deliberately left in place', horizon 15 explicit-scoped-restore) against implicit behavior
getTabState stays strictly read-only per its horizon-7 binding decision; closeSandboxTab is a new PAGE_ACTION, not a change to getTabState

Byte-size caps for readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests are explicitly deferred (dropped from this horizon's scope at the user's request during the Alignment Preview) even though they currently have zero size cap; this is intentional, not an oversight
closeSandboxTab reuses the existing generic onTabRemoved listener (capture-ports.ts) for capture-buffer eviction rather than duplicating that cleanup logic
risks: executeScript and evaluatePage use different transports (chrome.scripting vs CDP) despite sharing one size constant; assuming transport parity without diffing the two oversize branches first could produce two subtly different result shapes under the same discriminant

chrome.scripting silently passes undefined for missing trailing arguments rather than erroring — if findElement's injected function turns out not to be the sole caller, threading the limits as arguments could leave a second caller silently receiving undefined limits

Adding an explicit closeSandboxTab action that resolves the tab id via a broader chrome.tabs.query instead of the existing stored-id lookup could close the wrong tab under a multi-tab-matching race; the roadmap requires reusing sandbox-ports.ts's existing lookup specifically to avoid this

A too-large outcome surfacing as isError:true at the MCP layer could be implemented by string-matching a generic error field instead of a proper discriminant, conflating genuine thrown errors with the new non-throwing oversize outcome — defeating the horizon's own design intent

The live-Chrome closing verification is the step most likely to be asserted without real evidence ("it worked") rather than measured (tab id before/after, actual isError:true response body) — every prior horizon's closing phase has required concrete measured evidence and this one is no different
outOfScope: Byte-size caps for readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests — dropped from this horizon at the user's request; they remain uncapped by byte size (only entry-count capped) until a future horizon
JPEG/quality downscale rung for captureTab (deferred per decisions.md horizon 14)
Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/activeTab permission) — repeatedly deferred since horizon 6
The persistent-CDP-session redesign (replacing per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach)
A second render-the-tab primitive consumer (virtualized/lazy-content reads, trusted CDP input)
Measuring the true AI-client image-block reject size (still-open blocker since horizon 4/13/14/15)
Any pagination/continuation retrieval mechanism for truncated/oversize results
Any change to captureTab's own image ladder mechanism or ceiling value
Automatic/implicit sandbox-tab closing on relay disconnect or service-worker suspension — explicitly rejected in favor of an explicit caller-invoked action
analysis.domainShapeReason: Developer-tooling machinery inside an MCP bridge (result-shape policy and tab lifecycle code) with no business entities a domain expert would recognize, consistent with vision.md's classification.

discoveryFindings.finding: CaptureTabFailureResult (protocol/types.ts:343-356) is { captured: false, reason, size?, limit?, floor?, attempts?, detail? }; only the ladder mechanism is image-specific, the discriminant+size/limit shape is the reusable pattern.
discoveryFindings.implication: The new shared helper generalizes only the flat-ceiling shape, not the downscale ladder.

discoveryFindings.finding: coerceExecuteScriptOutcome (page-actions.ts:648-673) throws/returns {error} over MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS; debugger-ports.ts:588-595 imports the same constant and duplicates near-identical behavior for the CDP evaluatePage path. Two existing tests hard-assert the current throw contract (page-actions.unit.test.ts:1983, :2110-2126).
discoveryFindings.implication: Both must move together or diverge; the two tests must be rewritten, not just one.

discoveryFindings.finding: Module-level MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES/MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS (page-actions.ts:99,106) are never referenced by the handler; the chrome.scripting-injected function (887-972) redeclares local consts (890-891) because it is structured-cloned into an isolated world and cannot close over module scope (documented at 883-886).
discoveryFindings.implication: The only mechanical fix is threading constants through as injected-function arguments.

discoveryFindings.finding: resolveTabId() (sandbox-ports.ts:50-109) lazily creates the sandbox tab via chrome.tabs.create({active:false}) and persists its id in chrome.storage.local under SANDBOX_TAB_ID_KEY (line 24). No chrome.tabs.remove call exists anywhere in tools/chrome-bridge/src today (confirmed by repo-wide grep) — closing is entirely greenfield.
discoveryFindings.implication: closeSandboxTab must reuse this existing storage key and lookup, and clear it on close so the next resolveTabId() lazily recreates a fresh tab via its existing fallback path.

discoveryFindings.finding: onTabRemoved (capture-ports.ts:34,49-53) already wires chrome.tabs.onRemoved to evict that tab's console/network capture buffers for ANY tab, per horizon 2's decision. It is not sandbox-specific and needs no change.
discoveryFindings.implication: closeSandboxTab should call chrome.tabs.remove and let this listener fire naturally, not duplicate its cleanup logic.

discoveryFindings.finding: getTabState (page-actions.ts:1225-1253) is a documented, binding (decisions.md horizon 7) READ-ONLY, non-mutating peek.
discoveryFindings.implication: closeSandboxTab must be a new PAGE_ACTION, never folded into getTabState.

discoveryFindings.area: no natural session boundary / pull-only precedent
discoveryFindings.finding: bridge-client.ts auto-reconnects on any disconnect (lines 115-154) — disconnects are routine, not session-end signals. decisions.md records repeated explicit-over-implicit precedent: horizon 2's pull-only capture decision, horizon 6's 'deliberately left in place' sandbox-tab decision, horizon 15's explicit-scoped focus-emulation restore.
discoveryFindings.implication: Confirms the user's chosen design: an explicit caller-invoked close action, not automatic cleanup on disconnect or SW suspension.

discoveryFindings.finding: handleToolCall (mcp/server.ts:135-165) special-cases only captureTab (isCaptureTabImage branch, 151-159); every other action falls through to a generic non-error textResult (line 160).
discoveryFindings.implication: A new branch is needed to flip isError:true for executeScript/evaluatePage's too-large outcome, scoped to just those two tools.

phases.name: Add shared oversize result helper
phases.goal: Introduce a small colocated helper that turns an over-cap byte size into a consistent structured result, plus a shared type for it, with zero behavior change to any existing tool.
phases.rationale: executeScript and evaluatePage currently throw on oversize results with duplicated ad-hoc logic; before either can be made non-throwing, the codebase needs one shared, unit-tested primitive (checkSizeLimit / buildOversizeResult + a SizeCeilingOutcome type) that both call sites will consume in the next phase. Building it standalone first keeps this phase's blast radius tiny and lets the size-comparison logic be verified in isolation before anything depends on it. The type is named SizeCeilingOutcome (not OversizeOutcome) to avoid implying captureTab's existing downscale-ladder sizing semantics — a one-line doc comment on the type must say so explicitly.
changes: Add a SizeCeilingOutcome type (flat ceiling result, e.g. {withinLimit:boolean, actualBytes:number, limitBytes:number}) with a one-line doc comment distinguishing it from captureTab's ladder-aware downscale sizing
Add checkSizeLimit(bytes, limitBytes): SizeCeilingOutcome — pure flat comparison, no I/O, treating exactly-at-cap as within limit
Add buildOversizeResult(...) helper that shapes a consistent non-throwing result payload from a SizeCeilingOutcome, generic and not coupled to any one tool's field names
Unit-test both helpers in isolation: under-cap, exactly-at-cap, and over-cap cases, asserting real values not just non-throw
phases.expectedResult: A new, fully unit-tested size-limits.ts module exporting SizeCeilingOutcome, checkSizeLimit, and buildOversizeResult; no existing file changed and no existing test behavior altered.
inputs: page-actions.ts:648-673 (coerceExecuteScriptOutcome, current throw contract to be replaced next phase)
debugger-ports.ts:588-595 (CDP evaluatePage oversize path, current throw contract to be replaced next phase)

rubric.label: SizeCeilingOutcome type is correctly shaped and documented
rubric.ruleStatement: The new module exports a SizeCeilingOutcome type with fields describing a flat ceiling comparison, carrying a one-line doc comment explicitly distinguishing it from captureTab's downscale-ladder sizing semantics.
rubric.passCriteria: SizeCeilingOutcome is exported from size-limits.ts, has fields unambiguously representing a within-limit signal plus actual/limit byte counts, with a doc comment on the type itself stating it is a flat ceiling result distinct from captureTab's ladder-aware sizing.
failureExamples: Dev names the type SizeCeilingOutcome with the right fields, but the doc comment just says '// size outcome type' without mentioning captureTab or the ladder distinction
Dev adds the disambiguating comment but places it on checkSizeLimit instead of on the type declaration, so hovering the type in an editor shows no disambiguation

rubric.label: checkSizeLimit is a pure, correct flat comparator
rubric.ruleStatement: checkSizeLimit(bytes, limitBytes) performs a pure, synchronous, side-effect-free comparison and returns a SizeCeilingOutcome correct for under-cap, exactly-at-cap, and over-cap inputs, treating exactly-at-cap as within limit.
rubric.passCriteria: Function does no I/O, calls no chrome.*/DOM/async API, returns withinLimit true when bytes <= limitBytes and false when bytes > limitBytes, with actualBytes/limitBytes echoing the inputs unchanged.
failureExamples: Dev implements the comparison as bytes < limitBytes (strict), so exactly-at-cap is reported as over-limit, inverting the stated boundary
Function is correct but declared async / returns a Promise unnecessarily, forcing every future call site to await a pure comparison

rubric.label: buildOversizeResult produces a consistent, consumable non-throwing payload
rubric.ruleStatement: buildOversizeResult takes a SizeCeilingOutcome plus minimal generic context and returns a plain, serializable result object shaped for a future non-throwing tool handler, without embedding tool-specific fields only executeScript or evaluatePage would have.
rubric.passCriteria: Helper returns a plain object built only from generic inputs, contains no hardcoded reference to a specific PAGE_ACTIONS action name or tool-specific field, and is unit-tested to show its output shape.
failureExamples: Dev bakes in a field like actionName:'executeScript' or an MCP content-block wrapper shape lifted directly from executeScript's current code, coupling the helper to one call site before phase 2 starts
Helper silently discards limitBytes/actualBytes from the outcome instead of surfacing them, so a future caller can't report actual vs limit size

rubric.label: Both helpers are unit-tested across the three required boundary cases
rubric.ruleStatement: size-limits.unit.test.ts exercises checkSizeLimit and buildOversizeResult with under-cap, exactly-at-cap, and over-cap inputs, asserting on actual returned values, not just non-throw.
rubric.passCriteria: Distinct test cases for under-cap, exactly-at-cap, over-cap for checkSizeLimit with real value assertions; buildOversizeResult exercised at least for the over-cap case with a shape assertion.
failureExamples: Three test cases all assert only toBeDefined()/not.toThrow() rather than checking withinLimit/actualBytes/limitBytes, so a boundary regression would pass silently
Exactly-at-cap tested for checkSizeLimit but omitted for buildOversizeResult, and buildOversizeResult special-cases withinLimit===true by returning undefined unnoticed

rubric.label: No existing file touched, no existing test behavior altered
rubric.ruleStatement: Only the two new files are added; no existing source file (captureTab, executeScript, evaluatePage, findElement, or their constants) is modified, and no existing test is edited.
rubric.passCriteria: File list for the phase shows exactly two new files and zero modifications to any pre-existing file; existing test suite passes unchanged.
failureExamples: Dev 'helpfully' refactors findElement's duplicated constants in this same phase since it's mentioned in the horizon objective, violating the zero-behavior-change constraint
Dev adds a barrel export/index.ts touch to wire up the new module for convenience, counting as an existing-file modification

rubric.label: New code follows repo TypeScript strictness and layering rules
rubric.ruleStatement: The new module uses no any, no non-null assertions, correct type-only imports where applicable, and stays a pure/self-contained utility without chrome.*/DOM dependencies.
rubric.passCriteria: tsc --noEmit and eslint --max-warnings 0 pass on the new files; no any/!/JSON.parse-as-T patterns; module has no chrome.*/DOM usage.
failureExamples: Dev types a field loosely in a way that passes a lenient check but fails the repo's strict lint rule
Dev imports a type via a value import instead of `import type`, failing verbatimModuleSyntax/consistent-type-imports in CI

phases.healerHint: When healing, first check whether the failure is about the type's doc comment placement/wording — the fix is a one-line JSDoc-style comment directly above `type SizeCeilingOutcome` naming captureTab's downscale ladder and stating this type is unrelated. For checkSizeLimit boundary bugs, remember exactly-at-cap must count as within limit (use <=, not <), and keep the function fully synchronous and pure. For buildOversizeResult, strip out anything copy-pasted from executeScript's/evaluatePage's current oversize-handling code (tool names, MCP wrappers) — it should accept only the SizeCeilingOutcome and generic context, still surfacing actualBytes/limitBytes. For weak tests, replace toBeDefined()/not.toThrow() with concrete value assertions for under-cap, exactly-at-cap, and over-cap, plus an equivalent buildOversizeResult over-cap case. If any existing file was touched, revert that change — this phase is additive-only. Run tsc --noEmit and eslint --max-warnings 0 against the two new files before resubmitting.

phases.name: Make executeScript and evaluatePage return oversize results
phases.goal: Replace the current throw-on-oversize behavior of executeScript and evaluatePage with a non-throwing structured result built on the new SizeCeilingOutcome helper, updating the tests that hard-assert the old throw contract.
phases.rationale: Both tools currently throw an error when their result exceeds the size cap, an inconsistent caller experience versus a normal too-large result the caller can branch on. This phase rewires the two independent oversize code paths (chrome.scripting-based executeScript and CDP-based evaluatePage) onto the shared helper from the prior phase. Because the two paths use different transports despite sharing the same size constant, the two oversize-handling code paths must be diffed side by side before implementation to confirm they truly produce an equivalent result shape under the shared helper, rather than assuming transport parity.
changes: Before editing, diff the coerceExecuteScriptOutcome oversize branch (page-actions.ts:648-673) against the CDP evaluatePage oversize branch (debugger-ports.ts:588-595) to confirm both can produce an equivalent SizeCeilingOutcome-based result despite differing transports
Rewrite coerceExecuteScriptOutcome (page-actions.ts:648-673) to call checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult and return the new outcome instead of throwing/returning {error}
Rewrite the CDP evaluatePage oversize path (debugger-ports.ts:588-595) to do the same, reconciling any transport-specific field differences explicitly rather than dropping them
Update the two existing tests that hard-assert the old throw contract (page-actions.unit.test.ts:1983 and :2110-2126) to assert the new non-throwing result shape
Add new under-cap tests confirming normal (non-oversize) results are unaffected for both tools
Do not wrap the surrounding success/error handling in a broader try/catch that would swallow unrelated failures (injection errors, CDP disconnects) into an oversize-shaped result
phases.expectedResult: executeScript and evaluatePage both return a structured too-large result instead of throwing when over the size cap, backed by shared-helper unit tests plus updated/added tests in page-actions.unit.test.ts.

rubric.label: Both executeScript and evaluatePage rewired
rubric.ruleStatement: The oversize branch of BOTH coerceExecuteScriptOutcome (chrome.scripting transport) AND the CDP evaluatePage oversize path must be rewritten to use the shared SizeCeilingOutcome helper instead of throwing.
rubric.passCriteria: Grep/diff confirms neither branch contains a throw for the oversize case; both call the shared helper and return a non-throwing oversize result of equivalent shape.
failureExamples: Dev rewrites coerceExecuteScriptOutcome but leaves debugger-ports.ts's CDP oversize branch throwing, having only skimmed it rather than diffing as required
Dev updates both but the CDP path returns a different shape (e.g. omits a field executeScript's path includes) because the pre-implementation diff was skipped

rubric.label: Oversize branches diffed before implementation
rubric.ruleStatement: The two oversize branches must have been compared to confirm they can produce an equivalent SizeCeilingOutcome-based shape before the rewrite, not assumed equivalent by transport-name similarity.
rubric.passCriteria: Evidence shows the two branches converge on identical field names/types for the oversize result, with any transport-specific divergence explicitly reconciled rather than silently dropped or mismatched.
failureExamples: The two rewritten oversize results have subtly different field sets because the transports' available metadata differ and the dev didn't reconcile them
Dev copies the executeScript oversize shape verbatim into the CDP path without checking CDP actually has the same fields available

rubric.label: Non-oversize behavior unchanged
rubric.ruleStatement: Normal (under-cap) executeScript and evaluatePage results must remain unaffected — no behavior change, no new throw paths, no change to the success result shape.
rubric.passCriteria: Existing under-cap tests for both tools continue to pass unmodified, and new under-cap tests explicitly assert normal results are unchanged in shape and value.
failureExamples: Dev incidentally changes the success-path return type signature while adding the oversize helper call, breaking type contracts even though existing tests weren't updated to catch it
The CDP rewrite accidentally changes error handling for a legitimately-different CDP failure (e.g. debugger detach) while touching the oversize branch

rubric.label: Both hard-assert tests rewritten and new under-cap tests added, all passing
rubric.ruleStatement: The two existing tests hard-asserting the old throw contract must be rewritten to assert the new non-throwing result shape, and new under-cap tests must be added for both tools; the full test file must pass.
rubric.passCriteria: page-actions.unit.test.ts no longer expects executeScript or evaluatePage to throw/reject on oversize; contains updated tests asserting the structured result for both tools, plus new passing under-cap tests for both; the test run is green.
failureExamples: Dev updates the executeScript oversize test but leaves the CDP-oriented assertions at 2110-2126 checking .rejects.toThrow() because it looked like a different module and was overlooked
New under-cap tests are added only for executeScript, leaving evaluatePage's non-oversize path implicitly assumed unaffected without a passing regression test

rubric.label: Only size-ceiling errors become non-throwing; other errors still throw/reject
rubric.ruleStatement: The rewrite must not accidentally convert other error conditions (script injection failure, CDP disconnect, invalid tab, syntax errors) into non-throwing oversize-shaped results — only the size-ceiling condition changes.
rubric.passCriteria: Code/tests show non-size errors still propagate as thrown errors or otherwise-distinct results, isolated from the new oversize branch.
failureExamples: Dev wraps the entire executeScript body in a try/catch that funnels any error into the SizeCeilingOutcome-shaped result, so a genuine injection failure silently reports as oversize
The CDP rewrite reuses a broadened catch block that also swallows a debugger-detach exception, misreporting it as an oversize response

phases.healerHint: Start by literally diffing the two oversize branches side by side, noting what data each transport actually has available before deciding the shared shape, rather than copy-pasting one rewrite into the other. Use the checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult helper for both, keeping the change scoped narrowly to the oversize branch only — do not wrap surrounding success/error handling in broader try/catch that would swallow unrelated failures. After rewriting both source files, find both old hard-throw assertions in page-actions.unit.test.ts (near line 1983, and the block at 2110-2126 — don't skip it thinking it belongs elsewhere) and convert each to assert the new structured result. Add new passing under-cap tests for both tools. Run the test file and grep both oversize branches for a stray `throw` to make sure none survived the rewrite.

phases.name: Thread findElement limits as injected arguments
phases.goal: Pass MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES and MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS into the injected chrome.scripting function as explicit arguments instead of relying on duplicated local constants inside the injected closure.
phases.rationale: The function injected into the page via chrome.scripting currently redeclares its own local copies of the match/text-length limits instead of receiving the module's real constants — a real platform constraint: the injected function is structured-cloned into an isolated world and cannot close over module scope, so merging the two const declarations is impossible; the constants must be passed as arguments. Because chrome.scripting silently passes undefined for missing trailing arguments rather than erroring, the codebase must first be grepped to confirm findElement's call site is the sole invocation of this injected function.
changes: Grep the codebase to confirm the findElement call site (page-actions.ts:887-972) is the sole invocation of the injected function before changing its signature; document the search and result in the commit/PR
Extend the chrome.scripting args array from [selector] to [selector, MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES, MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS] at the call site
Update the injected function's parameter list to accept the two limits as arguments, explicitly typed as number
Remove the duplicated local const declarations inside the injected function (lines 890-891), including any fallback default
Update page-actions.unit.test.ts:622-668 to import and assert against the real module constants instead of hardcoded literals 50/500, in both the match-count and text-length assertions
phases.expectedResult: findElement's injected page function receives its limits as explicit arguments sourced from the module constants, with no duplicated local declarations and tests asserting against the constants rather than magic numbers.
inputs: page-actions.ts:887-972 (findElement call site and injected function)

Developer greps only the literal function name but the function is passed inline/anonymously, so the grep trivially returns one hit while missing an equivalent duplicated closure defined elsewhere

failureExamples: Developer removes the local consts but forgets to extend the args array, leaving the new parameters silently bound to undefined at runtime
Developer passes the constants in the wrong order relative to the parameter list, swapping match-count and text-length semantics with no type error since both are numbers

rubric.label: Duplicated local declarations removed

rubric.passCriteria: Reading the injected function body shows no re-declared local consts for these limits — all usages reference the parameter names directly.
failureExamples: Developer leaves the old local consts in place as a 'safety fallback' (e.g. const X = arg ?? 50), reintroducing the exact duplication the phase eliminates
Developer renames the parameters but leaves one stray reference to the original const name inside a nested helper, causing a ReferenceError on a rarely-hit branch

rubric.ruleStatement: MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES and MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS keep their module-level declarations and the call site reads its args from those same constants — no new hardcoded numeric literals at the call site.
rubric.passCriteria: The args array entries are the constant identifiers, not numeric literals typed inline.
failureExamples: Developer inlines the numbers at the call site (args: [selector, 50, 500]), silently desyncing if the constants ever change

rubric.passCriteria: The test file imports the two constants and uses those identifiers in assertions everywhere the old hardcoded literals previously appeared; no bare magic numbers duplicate the limit values in the affected test block.

phases.name: Close the sandbox tab on request
phases.goal: Add a new closeSandboxTab page action that closes the current sandbox tab and clears its persisted id, so the tab no longer stays open indefinitely and the next page action lazily recreates a fresh one.
phases.rationale: The single dedicated sandbox tab this extension drives all page actions through is created lazily but never closed anywhere in the codebase (repo-wide grep confirmed no existing chrome.tabs.remove call). This is an explicit MCP-caller-invoked action, not automatic cleanup on disconnect/suspend, matching the project's established pull-only/caller-driven precedent — the user explicitly chose this over automatic cleanup after discovery showed disconnects are routine/transient and SW suspension is undetectable. getTabState is a documented read-only peek and must not be overloaded with mutation, so this is a new PAGE_ACTION. The close call intentionally reuses the existing generic onTabRemoved listener (capture-ports.ts) for capture-buffer eviction rather than duplicating that cleanup logic.
changes: Add 'closeSandboxTab' to the PAGE_ACTIONS tuple (20 -> 21 entries)
Add params/result types to protocol/types.ts for closeSandboxTab, result shape {closed: boolean, hadTab: boolean}

Implement the handler: resolve the current stored sandboxTabId (reusing sandbox-ports.ts's existing lookup, not a new chrome.tabs.query), call chrome.tabs.remove on it if present inside a try/catch so an already-closed/stale tab id never surfaces as a thrown error, letting the existing onTabRemoved listener evict capture buffers naturally
Clear the persisted SANDBOX_TAB_ID_KEY from chrome.storage.local as part of closing, so the next resolveTabId() call falls through to its existing lazy-create path
Make the handler non-throwing and no-op-safe: {hadTab:false, closed:false} when no tab is currently open; calling twice in a row is safe
